ja: 店長が新しい企画、すごくいいって言ってくれて、めっちゃ嬉しかった。
en: I was so happy when the manager told me the new plan was really good.
alternatives: I was really happy when the manager said the new plan was great.
It made me so happy when the manager told me the new plan was really good.
point: told me の後は時制を合わせて is ではなく was

ja: 上司に本当の気持ちを伝えたほうがいいと思うよ。
en: I think you should tell your boss how you really feel.
alternatives: I think you should tell your boss what you really think.
I think you should let your boss know how you really feel.
point: 「気持ち」は how you feel と節で表すと自然

ja: 最近ずっと夜よく眠れてなくて、正直ちょっと参ってきてるんだ。
en: I haven't been sleeping well lately, and to be honest, it's kind of wearing me down.
alternatives: I haven't been sleeping well recently, and honestly, it's kind of getting to me.
I haven't been getting much sleep lately, and to be honest, it's wearing me down a bit.
point: 「最近ずっと〜してない」は haven't been ~ing で継続を出す

ja: 彼女、今朝からずっと機嫌が悪いんだよね。
en: She's been in a bad mood since this morning.
alternatives: She has been grumpy since this morning.
She's been in a bad mood all morning.
point: 「今朝からずっと」は is ではなく has been で表す

ja: 彼は転職を考えているみたいだけど、今辞めるのはもったいないと私は思う。
en: He seems to be thinking about changing jobs, but I think quitting now would be a waste.
alternatives: It looks like he's considering changing jobs, but I think it'd be a shame to quit now.
He seems to be thinking of switching jobs, but I think quitting now would be a waste.
point: about の後は動名詞 changing、主語の「辞めるのは」も quitting

ja: 母がいちばん喜んだのは、孫たちからの手書きの手紙でした。
en: It was the handwritten letters from her grandchildren that made my mother happiest.
alternatives: What made my mother happiest was the handwritten letters from her grandchildren.
The handwritten letters from her grandchildren were what made my mother happiest.
point: 強調したい部分を It was と that で挟む

ja: もし宝くじで1億円当たったら、あなたは仕事を辞める？それとも続ける？
en: If you won a hundred million yen in the lottery, would you quit your job or keep working?
alternatives: Would you quit your job or keep working if you won a hundred million yen in the lottery?
If you won a hundred million yen in the lottery, would you quit or keep your job?
point: ありえない仮定は if 節を過去形、主節を would にする

ja: 私、今すごく緊張してる。
en: I'm feeling really nervous right now.
alternatives: I'm getting really nervous now.
I'm so nervous right now.
point: 「今〜な気分」は feel を進行形にして I'm feeling とできる

ja: 昨日の映画、どうして気に入らなかったの？
en: Why didn't you like the movie yesterday?
alternatives: Why didn't you like yesterday's movie?
Why didn't you enjoy the movie yesterday?
point: 過去の否定疑問は Why didn't you のあと動詞は原形

ja: あんなこと言うべきじゃなかったな。彼女、きっと傷ついたと思う。
en: I shouldn't have said that. She must have been hurt.
alternatives: I shouldn't have said something like that. She must have been hurt.
I shouldn't have said that. I bet she was hurt.
point: 過去への後悔は shouldn't have、過去の推量は must have

ja: 正直、隣の席で電話している男の人に、ちょっとイライラしています。
en: To be honest, I'm a bit annoyed by the man talking on the phone in the seat next to me.
alternatives: Honestly, the man talking on the phone in the next seat is annoying me a little.
Honestly, I'm a little irritated by the guy talking on his phone in the seat next to me.
point: 「電話している男の人」は the man talking on the phone と後ろから修飾

ja: 姉は合格通知をじっと見つめたまま、受かったのが信じられない様子で 1 時間も座っていた。
en: My sister sat there for an hour, staring at the acceptance letter, unable to believe she'd actually gotten in.
alternatives: My sister sat there for a whole hour staring at her acceptance letter, as if she couldn't believe she'd passed.
For an hour, my sister just sat there staring at the acceptance letter, not believing she'd gotten in.
point: 「〜したまま」は , staring のように ing 形で後ろに続ける

ja: 前もって言ってくれていたら、空港まで迎えに行けたのに。残念だよ。
en: If you'd told me beforehand, I could have picked you up at the airport. It's a shame.
alternatives: If you had let me know in advance, I could've picked you up at the airport. What a shame.
It's too bad. If you'd told me ahead of time, I could have come to get you at the airport.
point: 過去の仮定は If you'd told と could have picked の形

ja: このお店、気に入った！また一緒に来ようよ。
en: I love this place! Let's come back again.
alternatives: I really like this place! Let's come back sometime.
I love this place! We should come back again.
point: 「〜しようよ」は Let's + 動詞の原形

ja: 正直言うと、一番がっかりしたのは誰も手伝ってくれなかったことです。
en: To be honest, what disappointed me most was that nobody helped me.
alternatives: Honestly, the most disappointing thing was that no one helped me.
To be honest, what let me down the most was that nobody helped me.
point: 「〜なのは」は what 節、「〜ということ」は that 節で表す

ja: 天気のせいで週末の予定をあきらめることになって、あなたはがっかりしてないの？
en: Aren't you disappointed that you had to give up your weekend plans because of the weather?
alternatives: Aren't you disappointed you had to give up your plans for the weekend because of the weather?
Don't you feel let down that the weather made you give up your weekend plans?
point: 「あきらめる」は give up。「〜することになった」は had to で表す

ja: 兄は口では平気だと言っているけど、本当はかなりがっかりしていると思う。
en: Although my brother says he's fine, I think he's actually pretty disappointed.
alternatives: My brother says he's fine, but I think he's actually really disappointed.
Even though my brother says he's okay, I think he's actually pretty let down.
point: although の後は節が続く。but と一緒に使わない

ja: 兄に無理やりホラー映画を最後まで見させられて、正直ちょっとムッとしました。
en: My brother made me sit through a horror movie, and honestly, I was a little annoyed.
alternatives: My brother forced me to sit through a horror movie, and to be honest, I was a bit annoyed.
My brother made me watch a whole horror movie, and honestly, it annoyed me a little.
point: 「無理やり〜させる」は make 人 動詞の原形。sit through で最後まで耐える

ja: コンサートが中止になったと聞いて、私はすごくがっかりしたよ。
en: I was really disappointed to hear that the concert had been canceled.
alternatives: I was so disappointed to hear the concert had been canceled.
It was really disappointing to hear that the concert was canceled.
point: 感情の原因は to hear、中止は受け身 had been canceled

ja: 昨日姉に、私が選んだ色はこの部屋に合わないって言われて、正直ちょっと傷ついた。
en: Honestly, it hurt a little when my sister said yesterday that the color I'd picked didn't go with this room.
alternatives: Honestly, I was a little hurt when my sister told me yesterday that the color I'd chosen didn't suit this room.
To be honest, it stung a bit when my sister said yesterday that the color I picked didn't go with this room.
point: said に合わせて「合わない」も didn't go と過去形にする

ja: 兄は、自分でもすっかり忘れていた誕生日を私が覚えていたので、すごく喜んでいました。
en: My brother was really happy that I'd remembered his birthday, which he'd completely forgotten himself.
alternatives: My brother was so happy because I had remembered his birthday, which even he had completely forgotten.
My brother was really pleased that I'd remembered his birthday, since he'd totally forgotten it himself.
point: 喜んだ時点より前のことなので覚えていた・忘れていたは had + 過去分詞

ja: 新しい職場でこんなに温かく迎えてもらえるなんて、夢にも思っていませんでした。
en: Never did I imagine that I'd get such a warm welcome at my new workplace.
alternatives: I never imagined I'd get such a warm welcome at my new workplace.
I never dreamed I'd be welcomed so warmly at my new workplace.
point: Never を文頭に出すと did I imagine の語順になる

ja: このワンピース、正直な意見を聞いてもいいですか？
en: Could I ask your honest opinion on this dress?
alternatives: Could I ask for your honest opinion on this dress?
May I ask your honest opinion on this dress?
Can I get your honest opinion on this dress?
point: 丁寧な許可は Could I / May I で始める

ja: もし彼があの仕事を断っていなかったら、今ごろもっと幸せだったと思う？
en: Do you think he'd be happier now if he hadn't turned down that job?
alternatives: If he hadn't turned down that job, do you think he'd be happier now?
If he hadn't said no to that job, do you think he'd be happier now?
point: 過去の仮定は hadn't turned down、今の結果は would be

ja: あの日ちゃんと話し合っていたら、私たち、今こんなに気まずい思いをしていないはずだよ。
en: If we had talked things through properly that day, we wouldn't be feeling this awkward around each other now.
alternatives: If we'd properly talked it over that day, we wouldn't feel so awkward around each other now.
If we'd talked it through properly that day, things wouldn't be this awkward between us now.
point: 過去の仮定は had talked、今の結果は wouldn't be と分ける

ja: この服の色、派手すぎると思う？
en: Do you think this color is too bright?
alternatives: Do you think this color is too flashy?
Do you think this color's too loud?
point: Do you think の後ろは this color is と普通の語順

ja: 明日の朝もまだ雨が降ってたら、家にいたほうがよくない？
en: Wouldn't it be better to stay home if it's still raining tomorrow morning?
alternatives: If it's still raining tomorrow morning, wouldn't it be better to stay home?
Shouldn't we just stay home if it's still raining tomorrow morning?
point: 未来でも if 節は現在形 it's still raining

ja: 新しい仕事、最初は緊張したけど、もう慣れたよ。
en: I was nervous at first, but I've gotten used to my new job.
alternatives: My new job made me nervous at first, but I've gotten used to it.
I was nervous at first, but I'm used to my new job now.
point: 「最初は」は過去形、「もう慣れた」は現在完了で

ja: 引っ越しの準備で困っていたとき、同僚が役に立つアドバイスをたくさんくれて、本当に助かりました。
en: When I was struggling to get ready for the move, a coworker gave me a lot of useful advice, and it was a huge help.
alternatives: When I was having a hard time getting ready for the move, a coworker gave me lots of helpful advice, which really helped.
A coworker gave me a lot of useful advice when I was struggling to prepare for the move, and it really helped me out.
point: advice は数えられないので advices や a advice にしない

ja: あの頃、自分の気持ちにもっと正直になっていればよかったって、今でも時々思うんだ。
en: I sometimes still wish I'd been more honest about my feelings back then.
alternatives: I still sometimes wish I had been more honest about how I felt back then.
Sometimes I still wish I'd been more upfront about my feelings back then.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を過去完了（I'd been）にする
